problem: Existing navigation maps (occupancy and semantic grids) record only obstacles or object labels, so they cannot search for an image goal by appearance. NeRF-based robotics methods (iMAP, NICE-SLAM, NeRF-Navigation) need per-scene optimization, do not generalize to unseen scenes, and are too slow to run inside a navigation loop.
motivation: Image-goal navigation in unseen houses needs a map that holds visual appearance, so the agent can reason about where a query image was taken and can correct noisy odometry. The authors observe that storing, in each grid cell, a latent code that decodes into a locally conditioned radiance field (as in GSN) gives three properties together: the map is visually descriptive, generalizes across scenes via a pretrained encoder/decoder, and runs in real time because mapping and localization never render.
key_idea: Build a 2D grid map whose cells hold latent codes produced by a pretrained RGB-D encoder and decodable into a neural radiance field. Search this map for the image goal by cross-correlating latent codes (no rendering). Use its differentiable rendering only for photometric pose tracking under odometry noise.
insight: Latent codes trained purely by an RGB-D reconstruction (autoencoding) objective turn out to be strong localization cues. Ablations support this. Removing the F_loc latent score drops the noise-free SR/SPL from 63.1/47.0 to 52.6/33.7 (Table 2). On Gibson-curved, latent-score-only exploration (59.2/43.4) beats occupancy frontier-style exploration-only (51.3/32.2), and combining both is best (61.4/45.6). Rendering-based camera tracking F_track raises noisy-setting SR from 59.8 to 66.9. With GT stopper information SR rises to 85.6, versus 61.4 for the full model, which shows the learned stopper is the main bottleneck rather than exploration.
method: RNR-Map registration (F_reg/F_map): a 4-layer CNN encodes a 128x128 RGB-D frame into per-pixel 32-D features. These are inverse-projected with depth, intrinsics and odometry pose into a 128x128 grid (25 cm cells, 32 m x 32 m), averaged per cell, and fused incrementally over time with count masks.

GSN-style decoder (F_dec): at points sampled along camera rays, latent codes are bilinearly sampled and converted to modulated-linear locally conditioned radiance fields that output density and appearance. Volumetric rendering produces RGB-D. GSN's upsampling CNN is replaced by a linear layer so individual pixels can be rendered. Encoder and decoder are trained jointly with an L1 reconstruction loss on the frames embedded in the map.

Image-based localization (F_loc): the goal image is embedded as a map m_trg at the origin. U-Nets F_k and F_q process both maps, and m_trg is rotated into R orientations and cross-correlated with the scene map. F_E (U-Net heatmap head + ResNet-18 head predicting 18 orientation bins) outputs a target heatmap. Training uses KL divergence to a Gaussian GT heatmap plus cross-entropy on orientation. For navigation it is trained to highlight the region closest to an unseen target.
Camera tracking (F_track): refines the odometry-predicted pose by gradient descent on the photometric error between a subset of rendered pixels and the current observation (5 Hz).

Exploration on a Voronoi-like graph: the occupancy map's free space is skeletonized into a graph. Each node's priority is its latent score (from the F_loc heatmap) plus an exploration score (ray-cast count of nearby unseen cells plus inverse distance). A fast-marching point-navigation policy drives to the chosen node.

Stopper: F_stop, a self- and cross-attention network over a local map crop and m_trg, predicts whether the agent is near the goal. SLING-style last-mile navigation then uses SuperGlue keypoints with PnP+RANSAC to estimate the goal's relative pose and approach it.

setting.backbone: Custom 4-layer CNN encoder + GSN-style NeRF decoder, U-Net/ResNet-18 localization net F_loc, attention-based stopper F_stop (all trained from scratch). Pretrained SuperGlue used for last-mile keypoint matching. Planning is heuristic (Voronoi graph + fast marching).
setting.training_data: 200 random navigation trajectories per scene collected in Gibson with Habitat. The main text says 72 Gibson training scenes; the appendix says 86 scenes (72 train + 14 validation). Encoder/decoder are trained first, then F_loc and F_stop on the frozen encoder. No RL; offline data only.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (90° HFOV, 128x128) + (noisy) odometry; goal given as an RGB-D image
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN LEFT 10° / TURN RIGHT 10° / STOP
setting.privileged: none (noisy odometry and actuation in main Gibson results; MP3D and some ablations run noise-free)

numbers_note: The main image-goal navigation results are on the NRNS image-goal dataset (Gibson val houses, straight/curved), not the standard Mezghani Gibson ImageNav episodes, so they are recorded under an 'other:' benchmark. Baseline numbers (DDPPO, OVRL, SLING variants, NRNS, ZSEL) are copied from prior papers. The MP3D split is not specified. Table 2 ablation values are averages of straight and curved: full noisy 66.9 SR / 42.3 SPL; no F_track 59.8/39.4; noise-free with F_loc 63.1/47.0; noise-free without F_loc 52.6/33.7. Object-change localization (50cm recall 97.4% at OC4) and novel-environment similarity results (CLIP 94.52%) appear in appendix tables. The appendix says training used 86 Gibson scenes including the 14 validation scenes, which contradicts the main text (72 scenes).
results: On the NRNS Gibson image-goal dataset with noisy odometry and actuation, RNR-Map reaches 65.7 SR / 40.8 SPL on curved episodes, beating the previous best OVRL+SLING (55.4 / 37.4). On straight episodes it has the best SR (68.2 vs 64.4 for NRNS+SLING), but its SPL is lower (43.9 vs 50.8). Trained only on Gibson, it transfers to MP3D-curved (47.7 SR / 35.5 SPL vs 46.7 / 30.1 for MP3D-trained SLING+OVRL). For localization it achieves 0.108 m ATE with tracking at 5 Hz, and image localization with 99.2% of queries within 50 cm in 0.018 s, far faster than NICE-SLAM.
limitations: Past odometry errors cannot be corrected once features are fused into the grid (no loop closure or pose-graph optimization).

Rendered images are low quality (128x128, small objects and textures lost). F_loc mislocalizes when a scene contains several visually similar places, and localization is limited to 25 cm grid resolution (25 cm recall 76.6%).

The heuristic point-navigation policy and the learned stopper limit performance (a GT stopper raises SR from 61.4 to 85.6). SPL on straight episodes trails NRNS+SLING. Training data per the appendix includes the Gibson validation scenes used for evaluation.
